lineas.texto: How does a ballpoint pen write so smoothly, without leaking all over your pocket?
At the very tip, there's a tiny metal ball, about a millimeter wide.
The metal around it is bent inward, so the ball can spin, but it can't fall out.
Behind it, a tube of ink pushes right up against the ball.
As you write, the ball rolls. It picks up ink on top and lays it down on the paper.
The ink is thick like paste, and when you stop, the ball plugs the hole. Nothing drips.
And that tiny hole in the side? It lets air in, so the ink can slide down the tube.
A newspaper editor named Laszlo Biro patented it in 1938, tired of smudgy fountain pens.
